explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/889: with v(n,k) the number of prime factors of n+k dividing none of n, …, n+k−1, is v₀(n) = max_k v(n,k) → ∞?  matches the page's definition, and v₀ is the ℕ∞-valued supremum over k. That supremum is finite for each n, since for k ≥ n at most one prime > k divides n + k. So Tendsto v₀ atTop (𝓝 ⊤) is exactly v₀(n) → ∞. Faithful.
